Networking.definition: A group of interconnected devices that communicate and share resources.
Networking.example: Computers connected to the same Wi-Fi network.

Networking.definition: A logical address assigned to a device to identify it on a network.
The fourth version of Internet Protocol that uses 32-bit addresses.
The newer version of Internet Protocol that uses 128-bit addresses.
A hardware address used to identify a network interface on a local network.
Domain Name System translates domain names into IP addresses.
Networking.example: Translating google.com into its corresponding IP address.

Networking.definition: Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol automatically assigns IP addresses and other network settings to devices.
Networking.example: Your router automatically assigns 192.168.1.5 to your laptop.

Networking.definition: A device that forwards traffic from a local network to other networks.
A value used to identify the network and host portions of an IPv4 address.
The process of dividing a large network into smaller logical networks.
Networking.example: Dividing 192.168.1.0/24 into smaller /26 networks.

Networking.definition: Local Area Network connects devices within a limited geographical area.
Networking.example: A network connecting computers in a university laboratory.

Networking.definition: Wide Area Network connects networks across large geographical distances.
Networking.example: The Internet is the largest example of a WAN.

Networking.definition: Wireless Local Area Network connects devices using wireless communication.
Networking.example: A home Wi-Fi network.

Networking.definition: Personal Area Network connects personal devices over a short distance.
Networking.example: A smartphone connected to wireless earbuds through Bluetooth.

Networking.definition: Metropolitan Area Network connects networks across a city or metropolitan area.
Networking.example: A network connecting different university campuses across a city.

Networking.definition: A networking device that forwards data packets between different networks.
Networking.example: A home router connecting your local network to the Internet.

Networking.definition: A networking device that connects devices within a LAN and forwards frames using MAC addresses.
Networking.example: A switch connecting multiple computers in an office.

Networking.definition: A basic networking device that broadcasts incoming data to all connected ports.
Networking.example: A hub sends received data to every connected computer.

Networking.definition: A device that converts signals to enable communication over an Internet service provider's connection.
Networking.example: A cable modem connecting a home network to an ISP.

Networking.definition: A device that allows wireless devices to connect to a wired network.
Networking.example: A Wi-Fi access point providing wireless connectivity in an office.

Networking.definition: A security system that monitors and controls network traffic according to predefined rules.
Networking.example: Blocking incoming connections from an unauthorized IP address.

Networking.definition: Network Address Translation modifies IP address information in packet headers, commonly allowing multiple private devices to share a public IP address.
Networking.example: Several home devices accessing the Internet through one public IP address.

Networking.definition: A logical communication endpoint used to identify specific applications or services on a device.
Networking.example: Port 443 is commonly used for HTTPS.

Networking.definition: A set of rules that determines how devices communicate and exchange data.
Networking.example: TCP and HTTP are networking protocols.

Networking.definition: Transmission Control Protocol provides reliable, ordered data delivery between devices.
Networking.example: Downloading a file using a TCP connection.

Networking.definition: User Datagram Protocol sends data without establishing a connection or guaranteeing delivery.
Networking.example: Online gaming and live video streaming commonly use UDP.

Networking.definition: Hypertext Transfer Protocol is used to transfer web resources between clients and servers.
Networking.example: A browser requesting a webpage from a web server.

Networking.definition: HTTP Secure uses TLS to encrypt communication between a client and a web server.
Networking.example: Logging into a website using https://example.com.

Networking.definition: File Transfer Protocol is used to transfer files between computers over a network.
Networking.example: Uploading website files to an FTP server.

Networking.definition: Secure Shell provides encrypted remote access to another computer.
Networking.example: Connecting to a Linux server using ssh user@192.168.1.10.

Networking.definition: A network protocol used for remote command-line access without encryption.
Networking.example: Connecting to a remote device through Telnet on port 23.

Networking.definition: Simple Mail Transfer Protocol is used to send emails between mail clients and servers or between mail servers.
Networking.example: An email application sending a message through an SMTP server.

Networking.definition: Post Office Protocol version 3 retrieves emails from a mail server, commonly downloading them to a device.
Networking.example: An email client downloading messages using POP3.

Networking.definition: Internet Message Access Protocol allows users to access and synchronize emails stored on a mail server.
Networking.example: Reading the same email on a phone and laptop.

Networking.definition: Internet Control Message Protocol is used for network error reporting and diagnostic communication.
Networking.example: The ping command uses ICMP Echo Requests and Replies.

Networking.definition: Address Resolution Protocol discovers the MAC address associated with an IPv4 address on a local network.
Networking.example: Finding the MAC address of 192.168.1.1.

Networking.definition: A formatted unit of data transmitted across a network at the network layer.
Networking.example: A webpage request is broken into packets before transmission.

Networking.definition: The maximum data transfer capacity of a network connection over a given period.
Networking.example: A connection with a bandwidth of 100 Mbps.

Networking.definition: The time taken for data to travel from one point to another across a network.
Networking.example: A 20 ms ping indicates a round-trip time of approximately 20 milliseconds.

Networking.definition: A condition in which data packets fail to reach their intended destination.
Networking.example: An online game experiencing lag because 5% of packets are lost.

Networking.definition: A network diagnostic utility that tests reachability and measures round-trip time using ICMP Echo messages.
Networking.example: ping google.com

Networking.definition: A network diagnostic tool that identifies the intermediate routers through which packets travel to a destination.
Networking.example: traceroute google.com

Networking.definition: Virtual Private Network creates an encrypted tunnel between a device and a VPN endpoint over another network.
Networking.example: Connecting to a company's private network through a VPN.

Networking.definition: A server that acts as an intermediary between a client and another server.
Networking.example: A browser sending web requests through a proxy server.

Networking.definition: A device or software system that distributes incoming traffic across multiple servers.
Networking.example: Distributing website visitors across three web servers.

Networking.definition: Virtual Local Area Network logically separates devices into different network segments on the same physical switching infrastructure.
Networking.example: Separating student and staff networks in a university.

Networking.definition: A seven-layer conceptual model that explains how network communication functions.
Networking.example: The seven layers are Physical, Data Link, Network, Transport, Session, Presentation and Application.

Networking.definition: A networking model that describes communication using four layers: Network Access, Internet, Transport and Application.
Networking.example: TCP operates at the Transport layer, while IP operates at the Internet layer.

Networking.definition: The process of selecting paths for data packets to travel between different networks.
Networking.example: A router forwarding a packet from a home network to a remote server.

Networking.definition: The process of capturing and analyzing network traffic to inspect transmitted data.
Networking.example: Using Wireshark to inspect DNS requests and TCP packets.

Cyber Threats.definition: A social engineering attack in which attackers trick users into revealing sensitive information through deceptive messages or websites.
Cyber Threats.example: A fake bank email asking a user to verify their account through a malicious link.

Cyber Threats.definition: A targeted phishing attack designed for a specific individual or organization.
Cyber Threats.example: An attacker sends a fake email using an employee's name and workplace details to steal login credentials.

Cyber Threats.definition: A phishing attack specifically targeting high-level executives or important individuals.
Cyber Threats.example: A fake financial approval request sent to a company's CEO.

Cyber Threats.definition: A phishing attack conducted through SMS text messages.
Cyber Threats.example: A fake delivery message asking someone to click a link and pay a small fee.

Cyber Threats.definition: A social engineering attack that uses voice calls to trick victims into sharing sensitive information.
Cyber Threats.example: Someone pretending to be a bank employee and requesting an OTP over the phone.

Cyber Threats.definition: Malicious software that encrypts a victim's files or systems and demands payment for their recovery.
Cyber Threats.example: WannaCry infected computers and encrypted their files.

Cyber Threats.definition: Malicious software that secretly monitors user activities and collects information.
Cyber Threats.example: A program secretly recording browsing activity and sending it to an attacker.

Cyber Threats.definition: Software that displays unwanted advertisements and may track user activity.
Cyber Threats.example: A suspicious application displaying continuous pop-up advertisements.

Cyber Threats.definition: Malware that disguises itself as legitimate software to trick users into installing it.
Cyber Threats.example: A fake software installer that secretly installs malicious code.

Cyber Threats.definition: Malware that independently replicates and spreads across systems or networks.
Cyber Threats.example: A network worm exploiting vulnerable computers to spread automatically.

Cyber Threats.definition: Malicious code that attaches itself to legitimate files or programs and spreads when they are executed.
Cyber Threats.example: An infected document that spreads malicious code when opened.

Cyber Threats.definition: Malicious software designed to hide its presence and maintain privileged access to a compromised system.
Cyber Threats.example: A rootkit hiding malicious processes and files from system monitoring tools.

Cyber Threats.definition: A malicious program or device that records keystrokes to capture sensitive information.
Cyber Threats.example: A keylogger recording usernames and passwords typed by a victim.

Cyber Threats.definition: A network of compromised devices remotely controlled by an attacker.
Cyber Threats.example: Thousands of infected computers being controlled to launch a DDoS attack.

Cyber Threats.definition: A hidden method of bypassing normal authentication or security controls to gain access to a system.
Cyber Threats.example: Malware creating a secret remote access mechanism on a compromised computer.

Cyber Threats.definition: Malicious code designed to activate when a specific condition or event occurs.
Cyber Threats.example: A program that deletes company files when a particular employee account is removed.

Cyber Threats.definition: The unauthorized use of another person's computing resources to mine cryptocurrency.
Cyber Threats.example: A compromised website secretly using visitors' CPU resources for cryptocurrency mining.

Cyber Threats.definition: Malware that operates primarily in memory or uses legitimate system tools instead of relying on traditional malicious files.
Cyber Threats.example: An attacker abusing PowerShell to execute malicious commands in memory.

Cyber Threats.definition: An attack that obtains the highest administrative privileges on a Linux or Unix-like system.
Cyber Threats.example: Exploiting a vulnerable service to gain root privileges.

Cyber Threats.definition: An attack technique in which an attacker gains higher permissions than originally authorized.
Cyber Threats.example: A normal user exploiting a vulnerability to obtain administrator privileges.

Cyber Threats.definition: An attack that attempts many possible password combinations until the correct one is found.
Cyber Threats.example: Repeatedly guessing passwords to gain access to an account.

Cyber Threats.definition: A password attack that tries words and commonly used passwords from a predefined list.
Cyber Threats.example: Attempting passwords such as password123 and qwerty.

Cyber Threats.definition: An attack that uses stolen username and password combinations to access other accounts.
Cyber Threats.example: Using credentials leaked from one website to access a victim's email account.

Cyber Threats.definition: An attack that tries a small number of common passwords against many user accounts.
Cyber Threats.example: Trying the same weak password against hundreds of employee accounts.

Cyber Threats.definition: An attack in which an attacker intercepts or potentially modifies communication between two parties.
Cyber Threats.example: An attacker intercepting unencrypted communication between a user and a website.

Cyber Threats.definition: An attack that makes a system or service unavailable by overwhelming or disrupting its resources.
Cyber Threats.example: Flooding a website with excessive requests until it stops responding.

Cyber Threats.definition: A denial-of-service attack launched from multiple devices or systems against a target.
Cyber Threats.example: A botnet sending massive amounts of traffic to a company's website.

Cyber Threats.definition: An attack in which malicious SQL input manipulates database queries due to insufficient input handling.
Cyber Threats.example: An attacker exploiting a vulnerable login form to bypass authentication.

Cyber Threats.definition: An attack in which malicious scripts are injected into web pages and executed in other users' browsers.
Cyber Threats.example: A vulnerable comment section displaying an attacker's injected JavaScript.

Cyber Threats.definition: An attack that tricks an authenticated user's browser into performing an unwanted action on a website.
Cyber Threats.example: A victim unknowingly submitting a bank transfer request through a malicious webpage.

Cyber Threats.definition: An attack that provides false DNS information to redirect users to incorrect or malicious destinations.
Cyber Threats.example: Redirecting a user from a legitimate banking domain to a fake website.

Cyber Threats.definition: An attack in which forged ARP messages associate an attacker's MAC address with another device's IP address.
Cyber Threats.example: An attacker impersonating the network gateway on a local network.

Cyber Threats.definition: An attack technique in which an attacker forges the source IP address in network packets.
Cyber Threats.example: Sending packets that appear to originate from a trusted IP address.

Cyber Threats.definition: An attack in which an attacker steals or takes control of a user's active session.
Cyber Threats.example: Stealing a session cookie to access a victim's logged-in account.

Cyber Threats.definition: An attack in which previously captured communication or authentication data is retransmitted to gain unauthorized access or repeat an action.
Cyber Threats.example: Reusing a captured authentication message to impersonate a legitimate user.

Cyber Threats.definition: A wireless attack in which a fake Wi-Fi access point imitates a legitimate network.
Cyber Threats.example: A fake airport Wi-Fi hotspot designed to capture users' information.

Cyber Threats.definition: An attack that sends forged deauthentication frames to disconnect devices from a wireless network.
Cyber Threats.example: Forcing users to disconnect repeatedly from a public Wi-Fi network.

Cyber Threats.definition: An attack that exploits a software vulnerability before a security fix is available or before the vulnerability is publicly known to the affected vendor.
Cyber Threats.example: Attackers exploiting a newly discovered browser vulnerability before a patch is released.

Cyber Threats.definition: A vulnerability or attack technique that allows an attacker to execute code on a remote system.
Cyber Threats.example: Exploiting a vulnerable web application to execute unauthorized commands on its server.

Cyber Threats.definition: An attack that manipulates file paths to access files outside the intended directory.
Cyber Threats.example: Exploiting a vulnerable website to access its /etc/passwd file.

Cyber Threats.definition: An attack that tricks a server into making unauthorized requests to internal or external resources.
Cyber Threats.example: Abusing a vulnerable website to access an internal cloud metadata service.

Cyber Threats.definition: An attack that exploits insecure XML processing to access local files or interact with external systems.
Cyber Threats.example: A vulnerable XML parser being manipulated to expose sensitive server files.

Cyber Threats.definition: An attack that compromises software, hardware or services through a trusted supplier or third-party component.
Cyber Threats.example: An attacker compromising a software update to distribute malware to customers.

Cyber Threats.definition: A security threat caused by someone within an organization who misuses authorized access, intentionally or accidentally.
Cyber Threats.example: An employee copying confidential company data without permission.

Cyber Threats.definition: A technique that manipulates people into revealing information or performing actions that compromise security.
Cyber Threats.example: An attacker pretending to be an IT technician to obtain an employee's password.

Cyber Threats.definition: The unauthorized transfer of sensitive information from a system or organization to an external destination.
Cyber Threats.example: An attacker secretly transferring a company's customer database to an external server.

Cyber Threats.definition: An attack in which attackers compromise a website frequently visited by their intended victims.
Cyber Threats.example: Compromising an industry news website to infect employees who regularly visit it.

Cyber Threats.definition: The use of malicious online advertisements to distribute malware or redirect users to harmful websites.
Cyber Threats.example: A fake advertisement redirecting users to a website hosting malicious downloads.

Cyber Threats.definition: A technique that hides data transmission inside DNS queries and responses, sometimes used for command-and-control communication or data theft.
Cyber Threats.example: Malware encoding stolen information into DNS requests to communicate with an attacker-controlled server.

Cyber Threats.definition: A targeted email fraud attack in which criminals impersonate executives, employees or trusted business partners to manipulate financial transactions or steal information.
Cyber Threats.example: An attacker impersonating a company's CEO and requesting an urgent bank transfer.
